content:
Hi all, I'm Jorrit. Background is in game tech & software infrastructure (CEO of a small infra/cloud gaming company) with a longer-running side interest in mathematical verification, particularly the question of how far you can push pure logic structures (kernels) built from minimal first principles on top of Lean.

I've been quietly using Lean for a while in my spare time and lurking here long enough to notice the recent threads on LLM-assisted formalisation. I'm reading it with an open mind and trying to understand what the community currently considers productive vs unproductive uses, rather than defending any side. Especially for deep kernel works, the trade off for using or not using diffusers/LLM's as proof/lean generators is interesting to me.

Hoping to start small with handwritten contributions in areas adjacent to category theory and operator algebras over the next few months. Will probably be in #Is there code for X? more than here for a while.

Thanks for the work this community puts into Mathlib, it's been impressive to lurk from a distance.

Just to flag that currently LLM-generated PRs to mathlib from new contributors are currently not welcome -- see https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html#use-of-ai . On the other hand, making downstream libraries using LLMs is definitely worth experimenting with.

Thanks Kevin, and quick /helpful reply. Indeed, I just read the thread regarding PR's, makes total sense. Will stick to handwritten work for any Mathlib contributions and keep any LLM/kernel experimentation downstream.
